title: "Light Out" at Midnight
hook: At 1:17 AM, the ALCS system reports a complete loss of airfield lighting control—runway and taxiway lights flicker and go dark. The AOC receives a garbled radio call from a ground crew reporting a 'random pattern' in the lights. As night operations continue, the pattern becomes erratic, suggesting a deliberate system manipulation.
threat: A cyber-intrusion into the ALCS server has enabled remote manipulation of lighting outputs, including false ON/OFF commands and altered intensity settings. The attacker used a vendor remote access tunnel (C6) that was improperly left active.

title: The Key That Still Works
hook: At 3:00 AM, a terminal employee is denied entry to the SIDA area despite having a valid badge. Moments later, a security guard reports a person in a maintenance uniform using a revoked badge to enter a jet bridge door. The system logs show the badge was revoked 12 minutes prior.
threat: PACS has been compromised via a cyber-attack exploiting an outdated vendor remote access tunnel (C6). The attacker manipulated the database to reinstate revoked badges, and the field panels are operating in 'Local Mode' (C5), so the revocation delay is in effect.

title: FIDS Gone Wild
hook: Passengers in the main concourse begin to panic as the FIDS screens display a fake flight from 2019, claiming a departure to Dubai. The announcement system begins playing a pre-recorded audio of a flight cancellation with no actual announcement. A social media post shows a video of a passenger yelling at a screen.
threat: The AODB/FIDS system has been infected with ransomware, corrupting flight data and displaying false information. The attacker used a phishing email to gain access to an unpatched terminal, then moved laterally to the FIDS server.

title: Fuel in the Wrong Tank
hook: A fuel truck driver reports that the fuel level gauge on the tank they’re about to fill shows 98% full—despite the tank being empty. The SCADA system confirms the gauge reading. The fuel farm manager calls the control room to report a 'possible sensor failure'.
threat: The Fuel SCADA system has been compromised, and a malicious actor altered tank level sensors to prevent overfilling alerts. The attacker likely used remote access (C6) to exploit a known vulnerability in the vendor’s software.

title: The Man Who Walked Through the Wall
hook: A security officer on patrol in the sterile area notices a man in a janitor’s uniform walking through a secured corridor, passing a TSA exit lane. The door appears to be locked, but he simply walked through. No alarm sounded.
threat: A cyber-attack on the PACS system caused a complete failure of the Fail-Secure door control logic. The attacker exploited a gap in the physical access protocol (C4) and manipulated the network to disable maglocks on SIDA doors.

title: The Unplugged Network
hook: The AOC receives a report that all airport computers, including the FIDS and ALCS consoles, have shut down. The network status screen shows the internet connection is severed. No one issued a disconnection order.
threat: The Airport Director authorized a network disconnection (C3) to contain a suspected ransomware outbreak. However, the IT team failed to follow the proper 'Disconnect' protocol (C3), leading to a cascading failure in manual operations.

title: The Ghost Gate
hook: A passenger is stopped at a gate near Gate C12. The system shows she is not cleared to board, but her boarding pass is valid and her e-ticket is confirmed. The gate agent checks the FIDS, which shows her flight has departed. The passenger is confused—her flight was scheduled to depart in 15 minutes.
threat: The AODB/FIDS system has been compromised, and the flight departure time was altered in the database. The attacker used a fake credential to access a terminal and then modified the flight schedule in the FIDS server, which is not integrated with the airline’s own system.

title: The Last 15 Minutes
hook: A security guard at the SIDA access point stops a man with a badge that was revoked 16 minutes ago. The system shows the badge is still valid. The guard contacts the ASC, who confirms the badge should have been blocked. The field panel is in Local Mode (C5), so the update lag has not yet been applied.
threat: The PACS server was compromised by a cyber-attack that delayed the update of the stop list to the field panels. The attacker used an active vendor remote access tunnel (C6) to insert false data into the access control database.
